The Stacking model outperformed other models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AVC. The Stacking method predicted the five-year survival rate of breast cancer accurately, enhancing prediction performance and generalization capability. Thus, the model is an effective solution for prognosis management.

articleTitle: Tongue Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning for Diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Tongue image segmentation is important in tongue diagnosis, oral disease diagnosis, and health monitoring in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Traditional image segmentation methods require a large amount of data with limitations. Deep learning methods, especially the UNet algorithm architecture remarkably perform in tongue image segmentation. We employed the UNet-based tongue image segmentation method and explored its application using tongue image datasets. The performance in TCM tongue diagnosis was verified in experiments.

articleTitle: Establishment of Information Platform for Enterprise Health Management Using Digital Intelligence and Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Health management in enterprises improves work efficiency and saves costs. Sichuan Shale Gas Exploration and Development Co., Ltd has actively explored a health management model and information platform construction with the help of digital intelligence. Based on the practice of the company, we described the idea, deployment, and framework of the health management platform. Based on mobile connectivity, the key role of enterprises was highlighted in the management of the employee's health. Using the employee health management platform, medical management was optimized to promote health management awareness and self-management of employees and monitor chronic diseases employees concerning employees's health.

articleTitle: Investigating Variances in Conductivity Contrast Across Different Frequencies by Electrical Impedance Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT), the intricate relationship between material impedance and frequency needs to be explored to implicate the precision and clarity of the reconstructed images. We delved into the complexities of frequency selection and its impact on image contrast, particularly on distinguishing between materials with varying conductivity levels, whether conductive or non-conductive. Furthermore, we explored specific frequency bands in which certain materials increase or diminish contrast within the reconstructed conductivity distribution image. Initial findings revealed that distinct frequency ranges influence the visibility of materials, suggesting potential applications for imaging specific tissue in EIT. The intermediary frequencies, notably at 25 and 50 kHz differentiate the characteristics of copper and resin. These frequencies facilitate a discernible contrast between conductive and non-conductive materials with intrinsic electromagnetic attributes. The observed disparities imply that the refinement of EIT imaging helps to discriminate materials with diverse conductivity effectively. Such results contribute to the development of EIT by addressing the intricacies of frequency-dependent imaging and allow for the understanding of material behavior in response to varying frequencies. Emphasizing the critical role of frequency considerations in the imaging process, future advancements are enabled to improve the precision and applicability of non-invasive imaging techniques, thereby allowing potential applications in diverse domains.

articleTitle: A Study of ECC Encryption in the Protection of Mental Health Data of Practicing Nursing Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With increasing concern about the mental health of practicing nursing students in the medical industry, how to collect and analyze mental status data securely and effectively is an important topic. Thus, we explored the application of Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) technology in protecting the mental health data in practicing nursing students. By constructing an ECC-based mental health monitoring system, we investigated the security issues in data encryption, transmission, and storage and evaluated the advantages of ECC technology in safeguarding the privacy and integrity of the data. The results of the study showed that ECC technology effectively improves the security of the data while keeping the system's efficiency and practicability. The challenges encountered in the implementation process and potential solutions were also discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Navigation of Parking Space Based on A-Star Search Algorithm Combined With Electrical Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the economic development, the number of vehicles in Taiwan is increasing day by day. When parking spaces are limited, a lot of time is needed to search for a parking space. Thus, we proposed a set of A-Star search algorithms combined with electronic tags in the multi-object parking space navigation (MOPSN) system. The MOPSN system saves the time of multiple users searching for parking space and reduces the energy consumption of vehicles, and the crystal beacon placement (Cip) method helps to reduce the deployment cost of electronic tags.

articleTitle: Deep Attention-Guided Hashing with Pairwise Labels-Geographical Information System: A Case Study on Tourism Development of Traditional Villages Along the South China Historial Trail
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The South China Historial Trail is an important heritage in the Lingnan region, China. By connecting the historical and cultural relics and natural resources of traditional villages along the Trail, rural tourism can be effectively promoted for the development of the rural economy. Using a multi-factor evaluation method, we constructed an evaluation system from five aspects: transportation convenience, environmental suitability, urban impact, tourism attraction, and regional population. Combining the analytical hierarchy process and multi-factor superposition analysis of GIS, influencing factors affecting the development of traditional village tourism was determined to support decision-making to formulate rural tourism policies.

articleTitle: Construction of Classification Model for Traditional Facial Color Diagnosis of Hypertension in Chinese Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Facial color diagnosis is an important method in traditional Chinese medicine diagnosis and treatment, with a rich theoretical basis and clinical experience. We designed an “Improved Multi-task Cascaded Convolutional Neural Network (MTCNN) Detection Algorithm” to define the facial color of hypertensive patients, and constructed a classification model for facial color diagnosis of hypertension using the Error Backpropagation Training (BP network) algorithm.

articleTitle: Integer-N Frequency Synthesizer and Sigma-Delta Modulator with Reduce Spurious Responses EMI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: An integer-N frequency synthesizer and a sigma-delta modulator were created and successfully implemented. The proposed integer-N frequency synthesizer includes of phase frequency detector, charge pump, pulse-swallow counter, and pre-scaler. The continuous-time (CT) sigma-delta (ΣA) modulator with a hybrid loop active-passive 5th order filter reduced spurious responses of electromagnetic compatibility interference and deleted the aggregate amplifier used in the chain of integrators with weighted feedforward summation (CIFF) topology employing the organization of capacitive feedforward.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control System for Water-Saving Irrigation of Greenhouse Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We designed a data collection and analysis system for managing air moisture, temperature, nutrients, and soil moisture in a greenhouse. In the system, a manager can monitor such environmental variables through the system's human-machine interface. The parameters are set according to the different plants planted, and the system automatically controls the plant growth environment. We also used image processing to judge the growth status of plants. The expected results were obtained by adjusting various parameters automatically to increase production capacity.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm-Based Melodic Optimization in Music Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligent technology, music education has ushered in new changes. Thus, it is need to optimize the process of melody creation by simulating natural selection and genetic mechanisms. As a melody optimization technology, a genetic algorithm was used to create diverse melodic patterns while ensuring melodic harmony and fluency. The algorithm enhances the efficiency of music creation, enriches the content of music teaching, and promotes students' musical innovation ability.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Stress Level Analysis Based on Skin Surface Temperature and Skin Conductance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In light of the negative effects of mental stress on health, there is growing scientific attention placed on understanding it better. This study aims to introduce a method that uses biological indicators such as skin surface temperature and skin resistance using easily accessible data to detect and predict stress levels. The publicly available dataset used in this study included the physiological signals of a group of university students whose signals were recorded by a wearable device during three exam sessions (two midterm and one final exam). Features were extracted from heart rate, electrodermal activity, and physiological and skin surface temperature and were input for the classification. In the labeling process, the stress levels were classified as high, low, or moderate. Machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) with classifiers were trained and tested with the labeled data The stress level of a subject was predicted with the highest F1 score of up to 0.8 and accuracy of higher than 70%. Such findings highlight the important role of skin conductance and surface temperature in estimating stress levels.

articleTitle: Exploring Perceived Hedonic Value of Intelligent Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The significant interaction between users and the hedonic value they perceived in the utilization of the intelligent wearable device was explored in this study. In-depth interviews and the KJ method were used with engage design experts, experienced users, and a wider user base of 510 respondents. Augmenting the recommendation features and real-time services bolsters the users' identification with the product. This result underscores the significance of these factors on user satisfaction, offering theoretical and practical implications from a managerial perspective.

articleTitle: PYNQ-Based Detection and Interpretation of Transplanted Positions in Rice Paddy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Taiwan, an island nation with limited natural resources, frequently faces extreme climate changes that affect crop production. An appropriate cultivation density of rice seedlings is crucial for agricultural data and economic development. With artificial intelligence (AI) technology, machine learning is becoming important for improving the accuracy of locating rice plants. Traditional discriminative deep learning algorithms identify or classify image data to estimate harvests of rice by classifying paddies with neural networks and designing loss functions. In this article, an algorithm was created to fit an orthogonal grid to noisy coordinates. The accuracy of assessing rice paddy positions was improved by using the algorithm. Utilizing field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), particularly Python Productivity for Zynq (PYNQ), deep learning algorithms on FPGA hardware were implemented using Python databases. The results showed enhanced aerial survey image recognition which addresses challenges related to power consumption.

articleTitle: Wearable Sensor Networks for Early Detection of Developmental Disorders in Infants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Diagnosing and providing patient-specific care for Neuromotor Developmental Disorders (NDD) at the earliest after birth increases the positive effect of rehabilitative interventions. Many qualitative, observational, questionnaire-based evaluatory tests carried out worldwide are mostly screening tests for at-risk infants but cannot assess their degree of disability. Thus, using wearable sensor networks and monitoring multiple kinematic motor parameters, we can identify patterns of NDD before the onset of symptoms, aiding their growth to improve their lives. Wireless Sensor modules of Inertial Measurement Units (IMU) (for spatiotemporal parameters), Flex sensors (for flexion-extensions, grasping, and gripping parameters), Photo- Plethysmograph (PPG) (for heart rate variability) and Force Sensitive Resistor (for pressure and force parameters during gait) are used to constantly measure specific parameters of movements such as reaching, grasping, crawling, and walking of infants. The movement data of adults showed a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) with less than a deviation of 2° from marker-based optical trackers. Implementation and tests of the developed network need to be improved to be fitted on infants. Doctors can provide patient-centric rehabilitative aid in infants' early stages of Neuromotor disorders by employing the affordable and easily deployable wearable sensor network. The network was proved to be better than conventional methods of using expensive technologies like Optical Motion Capture (Mo-Cap) cameras.

articleTitle: Entropy Weight Method to Evaluate Literary Tourism of Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Historical and cultural cities in China have profound cultural heritage and significant historical events. Using the entropy weight method, we constructed an evaluation system for literary tourism and evaluated the nature of literary tourism in 10 well-known ancient capitals in China. In historical time and space, urban development resources, and urban development status, the entropy weight method was used to calculate the weight of six factors. The scores of each city's indicators were calculated based on the city's data, and the literary tourism nature of the ten ancient capitals was obtained. The impact of urban history and the number of capitals was limited. Popularity in literature tourism was correlated, and the number of heritage sites and transportation efficiency were highly correlated. In Beijing and Chengdu, the nature of tourism was strong, while in Xi'an, Nanjing, and Luoyang, that was medium. It was weak in Hangzhou, Zhengzhou, Kaifeng, Anyang, and Datong,

articleTitle: Congruency Effect During Attention Network Task for Electroencephalogram-Based Alpha Neurofeedback Training
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: A bstract-Neurofeedback Training (NFT) using Electroencephalogram (EEG) allows individuals to self-regulate the activity of their brain non-invasively. NFT improves an individual's attention levels but the effect of congruency (alternation and repetition) on brain activity is still unknown. This study aimed to investigate the congruency effect of attention on 50 healthy participants (NFT Group: 25., Control Group: 25) after long-term alpha NFT. We examined changes in functional connectivity and band power within the alpha band. During the Attention Network Task (ANT)., each participant's EEG was recorded with congruent and incongruent stimuli in a pseudorandom order. A pre to post-NFT was increased in alpha band peak power within the temporal., parietal., and occipital regions., indicating the effectiveness of NFT. Additionally., there was an increase in task-related peak functional connectivity. However., the congruency did not affect the strength of functional connections between different brain regions. Stimuli alternation had a greater effect on alpha band power and connectivity modulation than stimuli repetition.

articleTitle: Identifying Fake Accounts on Social Media Using Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We proposed a multimodal machine learning approach to identify fake accounts on social media platforms. First, we employed Support Vector Machine (SVM) to analyze the activity status of individual accounts and detect potentially anomalous account behaviors. In addition, we trained Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to explore the relationship structure among accounts. Through Graph Neural Networks, we captured the complex interaction patterns and associations among social media accounts. Finally, by integrating both models, the accuracy of identifying fake accounts was increased. Through such a machine learning approach, the relationships among social media accounts were analyzed effectively. The proposed model achieved an accuracy rate of 81.1 % for fake account detection, outperforming that of a pure SVM model.

articleTitle: Speaker Identification for Detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Bilingual Voice Recordings of Picture Description Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: For the detection of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), we study speaker identification based on unsupervised learning with clustering. The voice of potential patients in picture description tasks was analyzed in Mandarin or English. The dataset included 67 Taiwanese and 62 English recordings. The speaker embeddings from Pyannote were used to identify the speaker type. We used three different clustering methods, namely K-means, K-medoid, and agglomerative clustering. To examine the performance of the clustering methods, we evaluated and compared the metrics of the silhouette score and the Rand index. Based on the evaluation of the Rand index, agglomerative clustering yielded the highest performance score for the clustering of speaker embeddings.

articleTitle: Future Electricity Supply Planning in Taiwan: A Dynamic Computable General Equilibrium Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The electric sector component of the Taiwan power sector model (TPSM) is a detailed generation planning model. The model supports power sector decision-making and evaluates the impacts of policy and technological changes at regional and national levels. In each time step, the model allows for capacity planning decisions and electricity dispatch arrangements to meet energy demand for various power generation plants. In the study, we constructed an integrated dynamic electricity supply planning model by incorporating a detailed dispatch and capacity expansion model of the Taiwan electric sector with a high-level dynamic computable general equilibrium (CGE) model. This model presents the least-cost deployment mix of power generation units subject to a scenario-dependent range of technological and policy constraints and energy input constraints. Various scenarios were simulated to show how changes in technology or policy constraints impact economic activities relative to a baseline case. The simulation results provide cost and performance data for renewable electricity system planners to use as inputs in their future planning and analysis.

articleTitle: Cluster Analysis of Effect of Social Support Using K-Means Algorithm on Learning Motivation of Primary and Secondary School Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We analyzed the relationship between learning motivation and social support among primary and secondary school students using the K-means clustering algorithm. Students from several primary and secondary schools in Province F, China were recruited in this study. The data on their level of social support and learning motivation were collected through questionnaires, and the data were clustered using the K-means algorithm to identify the characteristics of the group of learning motivation under different levels of social support. The level of social support was significantly related to academic motivation, and student groups with different levels of social support showed significant differences in academic motivation. Student groups with high social support demonstrated higher academic motivation, while the opposite was observed for student groups with low social support. The findings provide educators with targeted social support strategies to promote motivation and academic achievement among primary and secondary school students.

articleTitle: Sports Medicine Protocols: A Comprehensive Guide to Injury Management and Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Sports medicine protocols are essential as they outline evidence-based approaches to injury management, rehabilitation, and performance optimization for athletes of all levels. These protocols serve as standardized frameworks for sports medicine practitioners to assess, diagnose, and treat sports-related injuries, as well as to facilitate safe and effective return-to-play decisions. We overviewed sports medicine protocols, encompassing key components such as injury assessment, treatment modalities, rehabilitation exercises, and return-to-sport criteria. By emphasizing the importance of evidence-based practices and individualized care, the result of the overview enhances the understanding and implementation of sports medicine protocols in optimizing athletic performance and promoting athlete well-being.

articleTitle: Deep Attention-Guided Hashing with Pairwise Labels Method: A Case Study on Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area from Perspective of Sustainable Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Resilient cities are a new model of sustainable urban development to address various uncertain risks and promote high-quality development. Based on the Deep Attention-Guided Hashing method, we collected data on sports venues, community sports facilities, urban sports development plans, participants, and disaster emergency response in 11 cities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, China. U sing the data, we evaluate the resilience governance of sports in the cities.

articleTitle: Pilot Study for Early Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Baby Cry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We developed an algorithm for the early screening of autism spectrum disorder using baby cry sound. We collected the sound using a smartphone application to record it in their daily life. We employed the Japanese version of the Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers (M-CHAT) for the evaluation of the autism spectrum. We built a prediction model for binary classification using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression. We evaluated the validity of the features as explanatory variables used in the model by cross-validation, and the accuracy of the file-wise prediction in the cross-validation was 0.63. This result proved the feasibility of the very early-stage screening of autism spectrum using baby cry.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Utilization of Electronic Medical Record System: Conceptual Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Thereis a need for healthcare technology to aid physicians in improving performance while safeguarding patient health data privacy. Electronic Medical Record (EMR) is stored and used to maintain patient health data as an information source. However, the use of EMR is still less effective and poorly integrated. Physicians have not effectively utilized EMR despite its significance in healthcare services. Such suboptimal efficacy of physicians' EMR utilization impacts the quality and performance of healthcare provision. Thus, we formulated a framework for evaluating the utilization of EMR systems. A literature review method and interviews with physicians were used to identify the different aspects of EMR evaluation. Fourteen articles were used to develop the framework for EMR utilization in this study. The evaluation framework encompasses human, technological, organizational, and environmental aspects. The human aspects were considered for physicians' characteristics when using information systems. Technological aspects should address EMR system requirements. Alignment is necessary in the organizational aspect when leveraging EMR. Government regulations influence EMR utilization as an external factor. By exploring how to evaluate EMR system utilization, various perspectives can be studied to provide a basis for future research.

articleTitle: A Study of Psychological Factors of Adolescents in Artificial Intelligence Scenarios on Green Guidance in Actual Travel by K-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study aims to explore the impact of adolescents' psychological factors on green guidance in traveling in artificial intelligence (AI) scenarios. Through extensive and in-depth investigation and analysis of adolescents' travel behaviors with advanced AI technologies, the complex relationship between adolescents' psychological state and green guidance is revealed. In the research process, we adopted the theoretical frameworks of psychology and traffic planning to more comprehensively understand and explain the response of adolescents to green guidance. The findings of this study show that the application of AI in green guidance significantly improves the willingness of the reason and consolidates the validity of the “high probability zone of green travel”. The results provide useful insights for the development of urban traffic planning and intelligent traffic systems, suggesting how to motivate adolescents to choose sustainable and environmentally friendly travel modes with accurate green guidance strategies. Future research is necessary to further explore specific psychological factors and optimize AI. The application of AI technology in green guidance can improve the actual effect of green travel.

articleTitle: Quantitative Assessment of Myosin State Probabilities and Force Response in Striated Muscle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The macroscopic force generated by a muscle is the combined contribution of billions of motors comprised of actin-myosin crossbridges that individually interact following the laws of chemical dynamics. It is a complex system producing net mechanical work from chemical energies i.e. ATP hydrolysis. However, the exact hierarchy of chemical reactions is still predictive and widely varied. While the rate constants for several reactions is the same as in vitro conditions, it is challenging to calculate the straindependent rate constants. The only viable approach is to posit plausible values and simulate them to determine the force response under specific conditions. In this study, a computer model was generated in MATLAB to calculate the proportion of myosin in different acto-myosin states for isometric conditions using the parameters specified in the literature. The effect of power stroke length was also incorporated in the model which was not captured in previous models. Common misconceptions, assumptions, and shortcomings of the previous models were reviewed, including different mathematical approaches to muscle contraction.

articleTitle: Understanding Stress in the Aging Community with Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Addressing stress in the aging community calls for heightened attention in patient care and mental health services. To refine our comprehension of stress, this study employed electroencephalography (EEG) bio-signal data gathered from individuals aged 65 and older engaged in various skill-based games. The g.Nautilus Research headset facilitated the acquisition of EEG data. This study's participant group included those without major health conditions; in future work, this data will be compared to others who are confronting significant health issues. Subsequent MATLAB processing enabled comparisons between EEG stress signals of participants without major health conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Group Tourism Behavior and Guidance Strategies Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Accompanied by the rising demand for tourism, the traffic in the road and scenic spots has increased, which causes safety problems. Through data analysis of different individual travel characteristics, the travel mode selection model was constructed based on the multinomial Logit model to identify the influencing factors affecting the travel mode. Three types of groups were classified based on the density peak clustering algorithm. By summarizing the information of the three types of groups, group travel guidance strategies and information were formulated, and group travel guidance was created.

articleTitle: Application of Edge Detection Technology Based on YOLOv8 in Smart Mobility Aids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Global aging presents profound challenges, especially concerning the well-being and mobility of the elderly. Fortunately, technological progress offers means for those with mobility limitations. With the aging population, the significance of the safety and accessibility of passive mobility methods becomes increasingly apparent. In this context, many individuals are using wheelchairs or other assistive devices to maintain their independence for daily mobility. Outdoor environments pose numerous challenges for wheelchair users, such as curbs, uneven road surfaces, and unexpected obstacles. These challenges elevate the risk of accidents and limit freedom of movement. To address these challenges and enhance the adaptability of assistive devices outdoors, we proposed a method by combining YOLOv8 for semantic segmentation with real-time edge detection of road scenes to accurately estimate curb positions. By leveraging the proposed method, various elements of the environment are accurately identified in real-time, including curbs and road conditions. Moreover, by calculating the distance between the wheelchair and the curbs, the system provides timely alerts and guidance to users regarding potential hazards or obstacles, empowering them to swiftly respond to their surroundings and avoid collisions for safety. For the elderly with visual impairments or declining reaction capabilities, the benefits of the system are significant. By enhancing safety, accessibility, and adaptability, the system revolutionizes mobility assistance and empowers individuals to lead more fulfilling and independent lives as they age.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Intelligent Energy Management in Vocational Colleges and Universities Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, its application in intelligent energy management is becoming widespread. In this study, IoT technology was applied to the intelligent energy management system of vocational colleges and universities. A series of control strategies were determined to optimize energy use, reduce energy consumption, and improve the efficiency of energy utilization. The current situation and problems of energy management in vocational colleges and universities were analyzed to design an intelligent energy management system based on IoT. The system monitored and analyzed energy usage in real time by deploying sensors and smart devices. The system allowed for the visual management of energy consumption and a variety of control strategies, including demand response, predictive control, and adaptive regulation. The system was verified for the effectiveness of these strategies in simulation. The research results can be used for the future development of smart energy management in vocational colleges and universities.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning to Predict Mortality Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been developed rapidly in recent years. Two of the most common deep learning algorithms are the convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM). Intensive care unit (ICU) time series data can be analyzed by CNN and LSTM. In particular, ICU mortality rate and length of stay are crucial indexes to improve the efficiency of resource distribution, facilitate the provision of improved patient care, and drive intelligent developments in medicine. By extracting 21 features and 6 statistical features from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-III public database, the ICU mortality rate was predicted in this study. The focal loss function and synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) were used to solve imbalanced data problems. In preprocessing, the original time series data were resampled hourly, missing values were treated, data were standardized, and balance techniques were employed to resolve the data imbalance problem. A model combining CNN and LSTM was evaluated. The mortality rate prediction yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 87.8 and 53.5%, respectively.

Author Keywords: medical information mart for intensive care (MIMIC)

articleTitle: Interpretability of Deep Learning Analysis Result of Intradialytic Hypotension Prediction Model with Recommendation Reports Utilizing Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) is a significant clinical problem during hemodialysis for patient safety and therapeutic effectiveness. To solve this issue, we used sophisticated deep learning algorithms to anticipate IDH to occur and improve dialysis treatment and care. We collected a dataset of 2,000 dialysis records from Annan Hospital and investigated numerous machine learning techniques, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), random forest, extreme random tree (Extra Tree), XGBoost, and optical gradient boosting (OGB). Machine (LightGBM) and Category Booster (CatBoost) improve the prediction ability of IDH occurrences. To accurately evaluate possible risk factors, we cleaned and prepared data, incorporating physiological indicators such as blood test data, and dialysis machine information. The model utilizes entropy and the Gini index to segment data optimally with locally interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) for the forecast. The area under curve (AUC) of the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) was used to assess the model's predictive ability with models such as LightGBM, CatBoost, and Random Forest with Gini criteria. The model demonstrated a strong predictive ability (AUC = 0.83). In contrast, the ExtraTree model performed worse. Using the feature analysis result, critical predictive parameters such as preexisting systolic and diastolic blood pressure, effective blood flow, and ultrafiltration characteristics were identified. The natural language processing capabilities of ChatGPT-4 and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) were used to synthesize meaningful clinical data.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Gesture Recognition in VR Games
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: An OpenCV-based gesture recognition technique was investigated to recognize user gestures by analyzing the difference between the cue shadows of the standard image and the user's movements in VR games. The innovative method was used to evaluate the similarity by calculating the Eulerian distance between the participant's action and the standard image. The developed method showed high recognition accuracy and real-time performance in a variety of VR game scenarios providing a natural and intuitive interaction experience for users.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Cost Laser-Induced Light Backscattering Imaging System for Food Quality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Nowadays, food quality control is an important issue. Consumers are increasingly concerned about the quality of the food. This requires different methods from the conventional ones in food quality assessment. Optical-based methods show high efficiency in food quality assessment, and the laser backscattering imaging (LLBI) technique is also considered a potential method. In this study, we developed a low-cost model for food quality assessment based on LLBI at a wavelength of 650 nm. The model was tested using 20 samples of Musa acuminata bananas at four different ripening stages: raw, unripe, ripe, and overripe. The backscattering images of the test samples were captured using a charge-coupled device (CCD Camera). The gray-level intensity of the backscattering images was used for the evaluation. The evaluation results showed clear differences in the LLBI parameters at the ripening stages of bananas owing to changes in the chemical components inside bananas over time. The feasibility of the methods was evaluated for assessing food quality in the food industry.

articleTitle: Credit Supervision System for Medical Institutions Based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We explored the architecture and design of the credit supervision system for medical institutions and proposed a design solution based on modular and hierarchical principles. The system architecture consisted of a data layer, logic layer, and presentation layer to achieve comprehensive management, in-depth evaluation, and efficient supervision of medical institution credit information. Key elements such as security, scalability, and high availability were determined in the design process to ensure the system can operate stably, reliably, and effectively respond to the growth and changes in future business demands. The results of this study provide a scientific and reasonable architectural design solution for the construction of the credit supervision system for medical institutions, promoting the healthy and orderly development of the medical industry.

articleTitle: Personal Credit Risk Prediction Model for Peer-to-Peer Lending Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The increase of Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending platforms has revolutionized financial services but has introduced significant risks, particularly concerning borrower defaults. This study aims to develop an advanced prediction model for the assessment of P2P borrower default risk using data mining techniques. We explored key concepts such as decision tree theory and Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) to build a robust prediction framework. The research results address the challenge of imbalanced datasets using data cleaning, feature engineering, and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). The model incorporates Decision Tree-based methods using the C4.5 algorithm and an ensemble approach combining Random Forest, GBDT, and Logistic Regression. The performance of the model was evaluated using Precision, Recall, F1-score, and area-undercurve-Receiver Operating Characteristics. The results of this study enhance prediction accuracy and managing risks in P2P lending and offer information for lenders and investors.

articleTitle: Intelligent Monitoring of Physical Training Based on Human Key Point Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The purpose of this research was to analyze the possibility of employing key point detection systems as a tool for exercising control. Procedures that have been used in the past require the assistance of trainers but are biased and expensive. Automated systems provide accurate feedback by focusing on individual movements and allow for increased availability for self-training and long-term cost-effectiveness. In order to analyze the similarity and effectiveness of these systems, we explored similar systems and how they worked for real-time feedback to enhance proper technique and performance and minimize injury risks. The automated key point detection-based system offered improved feedback and early warning for potential injuries. Thus, despite high costs presently, the system is complex but effective, which allows the system to be used soon.

articleTitle: Impact of Backpack on Walking Gait
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Load carriage is common in daily activities. Excessive load carriage leads to postural alteration, discomfort, and potential injuries. A variety of bags are available in the market, with certain bags featuring ergonomic designs to mitigate the effects of heavy load carriage. We explored how various backpack designs and differing load levels influence the postural biomechanics of young adults' walking gait. We collected data from 20 female university students (22 ± 1 years old, 161 ± 6 cm, and 52 ± 6 kg), and we analyzed parameters including cadence, step length, stride length, trunk flexion angle, ankle, knee and pelvic range of motion (tilt, obliquity, rotation), as well as vertical ground reaction force. The results indicated that variations in load carriage bags did not significantly influence the spatiotemporal parameters but the quantity of loads carried impacted vertical ground reaction force, trunk flexion angle, and pelvic obliquity (p < 0.05). Notably, no significant difference was observed between the ergonomic and traditional backpacks, which raises questions about marketing claims that suggest substantial weight reduction, particularly concerning vertical ground reaction force. However, ergonomic backpacks did significantly reduce trunk flexion angle (p < 0.05). Such finding allows for a better understanding of how load carriage affects walking gait and serves as a guide for evaluating the importance of backpack design.

articleTitle: EcoSmartGuide: Language Learning Model and Retrieval-Augmented Generation-Based Platform for Streamlined Environmental, Social, and Governance Information Access and Report Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: EcoSmartGuide leverages the Language Learning Model (LLM) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based (RAG) architectures to streamline Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting, automating data aggregation and analysis. It shows a citation accuracy of 95% in reflecting ESG metrics and a coverage rate of 76.23% in the representation of ESG performance. Stakeholder feedback indicates high user satisfaction and improved decision-making processes. In a case study, EcoSmartGuide's effectiveness is demonstrated in identifying overlooked risks and enhancing decisions. The platform showcases AI's transformative potential in sustainability reporting and decision-making efficiently and accurately. Future research is needed to prioritize longitudinal studies, technological advancements, and diverse industry applications to ensure broader applicability and relevance.

articleTitle: Cell-Cell Communication Through Deformation of Extracellular Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Understanding cell-cell communication in cancer is important because cancer cells communicate to facilitate collective migration, such as during cancer progression and metastasis. We investigated how cancer cells communicate to facilitate their collective motion. We considered two major modes of cell-cell communication: chemical and mechanical. The results showed that chemical communication through specific signal molecules investigated in this study is not the only communication mechanism. Additionally, an aggregate of cells deforms their surrounding ECM, enabling mechanical communication.

articleTitle: Utilizing Recurrent Neural Network for Deepfake Video Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In recent years, deepfake technology has been significantly advanced, making fake videos increasingly difficult to distinguish. The face-manipulated videos have been used to interfere with political elections and impact personal reputations, threatening social and individual safety. Thus, deepfake video detection technology is essential as a countermeasure against deepfakes. Recent studies have demonstrated that spatiotemporal feature analysis is useful in identifying fake videos. Based on the result, we trained residual neural networks for facial feature extraction and recurrent neural network for temporal feature processing using three well-known datasets. We also designed a user interface to allow users to upload videos for recognition, and in response, provide a binary prediction outcome. The entire model architecture was validated with an accuracy of 85% and an F1 Score of 0.9 for predicting deepfake videos.

articleTitle: Interactive Visualization of Big Data of City Using Stream Smoothing and Generating Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Interactive visualization is critical in visualization research, propelled by advancements in simulation data, innovative interaction devices, and evolving visualization interaction requirements. Interactive visualization has been paid much attention due to its potential to transform data and user engagement. Air transport has cemented its role as a vital mode of transport for passengers and cargo, significantly influencing regional urban systems. The position of a city in the global or national aviation network is a direct indicator of its rank in the global or national urban hierarchy. This network, consisting of nodes (airports) and lines (airlines), not only facilitates spatial accessibility among cities but also intuitively reflects the hierarchical structure and distribution pattern of the national urban system. Despite advancements, data visualization, particularly its application to air transport faces challenges such as cluttering, the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem (MAUP), and data normalization. To address these challenges, we explored web-access information through the visualization of its inherent large datasets, utilizing a stream smoothing and generating algorithm (SSGA). This approach begins with a review of methods for spatial interaction in visualization. Following this, a method is selected and applied to the dataset concerning aircraft flight flow in China. The method's effectiveness in handling spatial interaction data was verified. The method helps overcome the challenges in data visualization.

articleTitle: Exploring Disease Insight Among Patients with Depression: The Role of Alcohol Consumption Frequency as a Mediating Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: In contemporary society, bipolar disorder and depression have become prevalent mental health issues. Despite patients often experiencing severe emotional and behavioral disturbances, a lack of self-awareness and insight into their illness prevents many from recognizing their mental health problems early. Currently, most academic research focuses on the relationship between depression and patients' insight or the association between depression and alcohol use behavior. However, there is a lack of literature examining alcohol use behavior as a mediating factor and exploring the causal relationships among these factors. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the causal relationships among these three variables, with the severity of depression as the exposure, insight as the outcome, and frequency of alcohol consumption as the mediating factor. Additionally, we employ regression analysis as the primary analytical method. The results indicate that: (1) an increase in the severity of depression decreases awareness of insight; (2) the severity of depression not only directly affects insight but also indirectly reduces awareness of insight through the frequency of alcohol consumption. These findings are significant for enhancing our understanding of patients' cognitive conditions and formulating relevant intervention measures.

articleTitle: Design of Elderly Walker Based on ANSYS Computer Simulation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Based on the living needs of the elderly, we analyzed the current development status of assistive products in the market and explored the design of the elderly walker from the perspectives of obstacle-crossing function, safety, and lightweight. Using ANSYS finite element theory, the stress and strength verification of three-star wheels made of aluminum alloy and carbon fiber were simulated and analyzed. Combined with ergonomics, the handle height, axle spacing, and other parameters were designed for lightweight, safe, convenient, and easy to push to better serve the elderly.

articleTitle: Deploying Natural Language Processing for Improved Patient-Doctor Communication in Gynecological Consultations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We deployed Natural Language Processing (NLP) to enhance patient-doctor communication in gynecological consultations and address medical jargon, time constraints, and sensitive discussions. Through a literature review, NLP applications were reviewed for understanding patients and supporting clinical decision-making. NLP increased the level of satisfaction of patients and clinical productivity. NLP technologies can be used to solve privacy and cultural issues. NLP can transform gynecological care and enhance communication and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation for Smart Medical Alert Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With the increasing emergence of Internet of Things (IoT) systems and devices., the concept of a real-time monitoring system., especially targeted towards the elderly., has existed for quite a long time. Most commonly., many elderly patients are typically at high-risk of experiencing a sudden medical emergency within an isolated room. As a result., various monitoring systems have been proposed which involve a wearable type of technology., or utilize a vision-based system in conjunction with a camera., which raises concerns of violations of one's privacy within their own home. As such., there has been a concentrated effort towards the construction of a system that has the capability for effective real-time monitoring of patients., while also being minimally invasive and non-wearable. Through the utilization of a wide combination of ambient sensors in conjunction with Bluetooth IoT technology., this system is designed to be non-invasive while still being proficient at the task of real-time monitoring of the patient's status within a room.

articleTitle: Head-Motion Based Interfacing for Actuating an Articulated Laparoscope with Flexible Distal End
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: A robotic scope holder's interfacing mechanism aids a surgeon in steering a laparoscope for visualizing the operative field for minimally invasive surgeries. We developed a head-motion-based interfacing mechanism to control an articulated laparoscope with a flexible distal end. Computer algorithms were developed to process the surgeon's head motion and convert it into actuation commands to control the robotic scope holder. These algorithms ensure surgeon's natural head motions are mapped to the movements of the scope distal end such that a first-person view of the operative field is always maintained. The evaluation of the proposed system was performed in a simulated environment. While tracking the target poses based on the operator's head motion, the shaft of the laparoscope stays within 2 mm from the incision point and the distal end of the laparoscope follows the target with 25 mm of the maximum lag distance. Thus, the developed interfacing technique facilitates direct and uninterrupted control of the laparoscope.

articleTitle: Exploring Cough Sounds in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Patients Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We classified respiratory sounds that indicate the early stages of coughing in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Deep learning techniques with a voice spectrogram were utilized for respiratory sound detection. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were applied to classify COPD by extracting features from the respiratory sounds. The optimized model achieved an accuracy rate of 91 %. Since the pretraining database was sourced from publicly available data from the Internet, the model was enhanced by incorporating COPD sounds provided by doctors as feedback.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Cladding Layer Depletted FBG Sensor and its Measurement of Solutions with Different Content
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) is popularly used for temperature and stress sensors due to its reflection which is crucial to the variation of ambient temperature and mechanical stress. However, there are fewer applications of FBG sensors to identify a liquid solution. When the cladding of the FBG is removed, the index of the liquid solution can then effectively change the index periodicity of the FBG. We fabricated an FBG sensor with the depletion of the cladding layer and the characterization of its wavelength shift to measure different sugar content at different temperatures.

articleTitle: Optimizing Patient-Manager Interactions in Chronic Care Using Generative Artificial Intelligence QA Dialogue Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Chronic disease management requires continuous care to prevent exacerbations, yet providing 24/7 accessible medical advice is a significant challenge for care providers. The current model of periodic patient visits with standard dialogue responses fails to adequately address the individualized needs of patients and caregivers. This lack of personalized guidance undermines treatment adherence and satisfaction. To bridge this gap, we developed a novel approach leveraging generative AI (GAI) to optimize patient-manager interactions. Focusing on prevalent chronic conditions such as diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and dementia, we created intelligent dialogue agents that deliver tailored, actionable nursing recommendations aligning with each case's unique circumstances. The developed methodology began by curating a corpus of 30 frequently asked questions on home care, emotional support, and social factors from online patient data across the three diseases. We employed prompt engineering to precisely define the virtual roles of nurses and physicians while implementing a “Rephrase and Respond” (RAR) protocol to enhance query comprehension and generate reliable solutions. The RAR approach solves problems by question restating, followed by contextualized recommendations from the language model. Clinical expert feedback iteratively refined the system's outputs. The evaluation result showed an average gain of 10% in response and an increase of 5% in readability after optimization. The optimized RAR method of large language models effectively improved the quality of nursing advice for chronic disease, aligned with patients' emotional and social needs. The RAR method in medical advisory areas, including chronic disease management and rehabilitation care, enhances the quality and practicality of nursing advice in these domains.

articleTitle: Insight into Fibroids: Cutting-Edge Detection Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We explored the forefront of detection strategies for uterine fibroids and integrated innovative methodologies to enhance diagnostic precision and clinical management. Uterine fibroids, common benign tumors affecting women of reproductive age, pose diagnostic challenges due to their varied presentation and symptomatology. Recent advancements in imaging technologies, such as magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and ultrasound, have revolutionized fibroid detection by offering improved resolution and tissue characterization. Additionally, emerging molecular biomarkers and genetic profiling techniques hold promise for early detection and personalized treatment approaches. These cutting-edge detection strategies were reviewed, highlighting their potential to optimize patient care through earlier diagnosis, accurate characterization, and tailored therapeutic interventions. By leveraging interdisciplinary insights and technological advancements, clinicians and researchers can navigate the complex landscape of uterine fibroid detection with greater efficacy and precision, ultimately improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction.

articleTitle: APP Design of Traditional Chinese Medicine Based on Affective Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Since the outbreak of COVID-19, Chinese medicine has greatly increased its international recognition for its excellent efficacy, bringing opportunities for the development of the traditional Chinese medicine industry. How to disseminate Chinese medicine culture in daily, regular, and trendy ways needs to be addressed. Based on the theory of emotionality and the medium of smartphone APPs, we analyzed the needs of users for Chinese medicine Apps at the instinctive, behavioral, and reflective levels. A mechanism was constructed for the design of Chinese medicine apps to meet the needs of users. A literature review and interviews were conducted to construct an indicator system based on affective theory. The Delphi method was used to collect the opinions of 20 experts, and statistical analysis was used to analyze the data from the questionnaire survey. The bounded-value method and the exploratory factor analysis method were also used to extract the indicators. 11 indicators in the instinctive dimension, 13 indicators in the behavioral dimension, and seven indicators in the reflective dimension were determined. Through a preliminary exploration of the evaluation of the APP design based on affective theory, a gap in existing research was filled to provide a theoretical basis for the APP for traditional Chinese medicine.

articleTitle: Voice Controlled Robotic Arm with Object Detection as a Feedback System for Visually Impaired Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The purpose of this thesis is to introduce a robot arm as an assistive technology oriented to the aid of individuals with visual impairment. The robot arm will sit at the center of a custom printed container to allow it storage of several items that will be retrieved when commanded to do so. The microcontroller (MCU) for the robot arm is an Arduino based MCU, ArbotiX, and is paired with a Raspberry Pi 4b for command translation, given that the commands for the device are voice commands, and will also serve as a processing unit for feedback systems. The voice command translation is based on Google Speech-to-Text API, and the two feedback systems to be explored are based on a weight sensor and object recognition under the YOLOv7 model. Experimentation has been conducted to visualize the efficacy of the robot arm in fulfilling its intended purpose and to measure the effectiveness of the implemented system for command delivery to the robot arm, and both feedback systems. The purpose of this robot arm is to aid individuals with visual impairment by retrieving, under voice command, spice bottles from its container and delivering it to the user of this device; thus, facilitating what would be a challenging task to a blind person, such as retrieving spices for cooking purposes.

articleTitle: Study of the Effects of Prioritizing COVID-19 Care on Preeclampsia Hospitalizations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The year 2020 saw the global community fighting the COVID-19 epidemic. To face the pandemic, the Ministry of Health of Ecuador ordered hospital reconversion for meeting the demand of care in patients with COVID-19. As a result, the “IESS Los Ceibos Hospital” was forced to suspend the hospitalization care of preeclamptic patients from May to September 2020. Thus, the present work considers descriptive and diagnostic analytics to study the effects that the prioritization of COVID-19 care had on hospitalizations for preeclampsia at the “IESS Los Ceibos Hospital” in Guayaquil-Ecuador. According to the results, there was a rise in preeclampsia cases over the seven-year study period analyzed (2017–2023). This growing trend was strongly interrupted by the prioritization of COVID-19 care. That interruption was also detected as an anomaly in the diagnostic analysis. Moreover, an average request of 67.92 hospitalization beds per month would have been expected in the absence of interruption of preeclampsia care. That detrimental effect that was statistically significant. All in all, these results have allowed us to quantify the effects of prioritizing COVID-19 care on hospitalization for preeclampsia, serving as a basis to avoid repeating drastic measures such as the total interruption of care due to the pandemic.

articleTitle: Task-Technology Fit Evaluation for Telemedicine: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Telemedicine is the delivery of healthcare services remotely using information and communication technology (ICT). To ensure the effective implementation of telemedicine services, the application used must meet users' needs and effectively support their tasks. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct task-technology fit (TTF) evaluation for telemedicine applications. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to identify methods used in TTF evaluation for telemedicine applications or other health information systems and to determine whether a specific instrument (questionnaire) for evaluating TTF was developed or used. The SLR corresponded to the PRISMA guidelines. Using combinations of keywords, an electronic search for relevant articles was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, IEEE, Wiley, ScienceDirect, Taylor and Francis, ACM, and Google Scholar databases. Search results were exported to an Excel file and screened by title and abstract, followed by a full-text review. Sixteen articles were included for systematic review. Of the 16 articles reviewed, none specifically addressed TTF evaluation for telemedicine applications. The objects being studied include telehealth, eHealth, and mHealth. The methods used in previous TTF evaluations included interviews, focus group discussions, observations, experiments, think-aloud protocol, mapping tasks to available technological features in a matrix, and surveys using questionnaires. Each TTF evaluation method has advantages and disadvantages. In existing TTF evaluations using questionnaires, most questionnaires were adapted from previous studies. These studies only made wording adjustments to the measurement items to fit the context being studied. TTF evaluation is context-specific so different contexts have different TTF measurement items or dimensions. No previous study has used or developed a specific TTF questionnaire for the telemedicine context. Further study is needed to develop such questionnaires by considering the specific tasks that users need to perform in remote healthcare services delivery that must be supported by technology.

articleTitle: Extinguishing Mechanism and Countermeasures of Lithium Battery Vehicle Fires
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: We develop an effective method for extinguishing lithium battery fires, which have become a significant safety concern as the popularity of electric vehicles grows. We tested seven fire-fighting methods, finding that combining a fire blanket with a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher was the most effective. Although water reduces the temperature, it also reacts with active metals and chemicals in the battery, causing further damage. We also investigated the rescue procedure in lithium battery fire and developed three types of fire extinguishing devices specifically for electric vehicle fires in alleys and underground parking lots. The methods guide local manufacturers to enhance public safety and support the fire brigade in Taiwan. Given that lithium battery fires are complex and pose unique challenges, the methods contribute to the development of new fire rescue equipment and procedures for firefighters.

articleTitle: Age-Based Predictive Modeling of Emergency Department Visits Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding, and re-source optimization are significant challenges healthcare systems face globally. Accurate forecasting of ED visits plays a pivotal role in proactive resource allocation and efficient patient management. This study explores the application of the Support Vector Machine (SVM) model to predict Emergency Department (ED) visits stratified by age groups. VMs are chosen for their ability to handle non-linear relationships and high-dimensional data, making them well-suited for complex healthcare prediction tasks. The goal is to evaluate the effectiveness of ML methodologies in forecasting ED utilization within different age cohorts, identify common reasons for visits within specific age cohorts, and assess the impact of age on the severity and nature of ED presentations. Age serves as a critical predictor in forecasting emergency department (ED) visits. For example, pediatric populations often present with acute illnesses and injuries, while older adults may have higher rates of chronic diseases and complex medical needs. By incorporating age as a variable, SVM models can stratify patients into different risk categories based on age-specific healthcare utilization trends. This allows for more accurate predictions of ED visit frequencies and resource demands tailored to specific age demographics. Furthermore, age-related temporal variations and seasonal effects, such as flu outbreaks or holiday-related injuries, can be integrated into SVM modeling to adjust predictions dynamically. Using The Nationwide Emergency Department Sample (NEDS) ED Visits data from 2006 through 2020, it is a comprehensive collection of data detailing visits to emergency departments (EDs) across the national scale. This dataset is specifically tailored for studying ED visits with a focus on age-related patterns and trends. The dataset reveals that the highest volume of ED visits over the 14 years occurred within the age group of 18–44, averaging approximately 158,056 visits per year. The machine learning (ML) model is refined through iterative optimization. Input data is processed by the ML algorithm, which initially computes model coefficients using an interior point optimization method. In subsequent iterations, the starting point is adapted based on the previous iteration, and the goal is to minimize the objective function, reflecting the difference between predicted and actual patient numbers. The model's impressive 96.7% accuracy shows strong predictive capability, while its high R-squared value of 0.996 indicates an excellent fit to the data, highlighting its reliability and effectiveness in capturing underlying patterns. The predictive model contributes to the efficiency of resource utilization and healthcare service quality by facilitating the identification and early intervention of high-risk patients, improved patient outcomes, and care management. This approach aligns with the broader goals of precision medicine and population health management, ultimately benefiting both patients and healthcare providers.

articleTitle: Toward Automated Meta-Analysis: Leveraging Large Language Model-Driven Outcome Alignment and Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Meta-analyses stand as a cornerstone in consolidating research findings to assess treatment efficacy within evidence-based medicine. Yet, they are often laborintensive and quickly outdated due to the rapid publication of new studies. On the other hand, harmonization of research outcomes reported in papers following clinical trials, is essential for ensuring clarity and consistency within the scientific community. These outcomes, often described using disparate terminologies by different research teams, necessitate a process of meticulous extraction and standardization to achieve uniformity. This standardization is critical for facilitating data harmonization, which in turn enhances transparency, reproducibility, and comparability across various studies. This study proposes a novel automated approach for the extraction and analysis of data from open-source research articles for meta-analysis. Utilizing large language models, our proposed system identifies and aligns semantically similar outcomes from various papers published subsequent to the clinical trials. The system further extracts pertinent statistical data, facilitating a more efficient and robust meta-analytic process. By automating the assimilation of emerging research, the system ensures that meta-analyses remain current and reflective of the latest scientific evidence. This method reduces the manual effort traditionally required and offers a continually updated, time-efficient solution for meta-analytic research.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Heart Rate Variability Error Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Convolutional Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) networks in correcting errors in the RR-interval series that is necessary for assessing cardiovascular health and autonomic nervous system function through Heart Rate Variability (HRV) parameters, i.e., time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear parameters. These parameters are used in clinical studies and medical diagnosis; however, errors in the RR-interval series, often arising from measurements in ambulatory conditions, use of low-cost wearable devices, and signal processing limitations, necessitate preprocessing and error correction. By employing Monte Carlo simulations, this study compares CNN-LSTM series reconstruction with error-containing series characterized by Gaussian additive noise and the traditional cubic spline interpolation method. Specifically, the RR-interval series were segmented into piece-wise stationary sections according to physical activity, and errors were uniformly introduced in 3300 samples in each scenario, with varying error presence (10% to 30%) and duration (Is to 7s) to assess the correction efficacy for different HRV parameters. The CNN-LSTM model significantly outperformed cubic spline interpolation (CSI) in reconstructing RR-series, with differences in key metrics such as RMSSD, MaxRR, HF, and LF reaching 98.12%, 98.80%, 100.00%, and 99.99%, indicating less variability and distortion. The CSI showed less deviation for alpha2, SampEn, and ApEn. While both methods show considerable differences compared to the erroneous series, CNN-LSTM more effectively mitigates errors between the erroneous series and CNN-LSTM reconstruction as the duration and presence of noise increase. This finding is valuable for enhancing the accuracy of HRV parameters, thereby supporting and improving medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Optimization of QFD-Based AHP Design for Sustainable User Experience of Wearable Medical Devices for Elderly
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: The needs of the elderly for smart wearable devices were explored and translated into design requirements to optimize the user experience of the devices. User requirements were collected through a literature survey and the Delphi method. The factor analysis method was applied to analyze the requirements. A hierarchy of user requirements was established using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) combined with Quality Function Deployment (QFD) to prioritize the requirements based on the weights and importance determined by the judgment matrix. The positive level corresponding to experts was 100%, and the authority level corresponding to experts was 0.86, indicating that the professionalism of experts is adequate. Cronbach's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> values were higher than 0.80 and the cumulative variance contribution rates of the three constructs were 86.89, 89.187, and 83.439%, respectively. The scale of user requirements includes two indicators of level 2 and nine items of level 3 for perceptual experience, three indicators of level 2 and nine items of level 3 for interactive experience, and two indicators of level 2 and six items of level 3 for value experience. The weights of user requirements and the conversion of user requirements by QFD showed that ergonomics, ease of operation, and reasonable structure were important design requirements. The integration of AHP and QFD was effectively used to optimize the user experience of wearable healthcare devices for the elderly, which is an innovative design to provide guidance.

articleTitle: Correlation Between Dielectric and Physiological Properties of Thrombi Based on Bioelectrical Impedance Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Thrombotic disease caused by thrombi is one of the important causes of death worldwide. The early detection of thrombosis may prevent cardiovascular diseases [1]. With the bioelectrical impedance technique, we determined the causes of impedance changes from the perspective of the vascular endothelial cell structure and blood components. We investigated the bioinformation that changes vascular and blood impedance and the correlation between the two, thereby providing a new impedance measurement method to detect thrombi. Through the establishment of a model of jugular thrombosis in rabbits supplemented by ultrasound to detect the size of the thrombosis model, pathological sections and hemorheological testing were created. The physiological changes in vascular endothelial cells and blood fluidity were observed before and after the lesion in the experiment. At the same time, an impedance analyzer was applied to collect dielectric information of vessels and blood to analyze the correlation between dielectric and physiological properties of vessels and blood. Electrical conductivity became higher with thrombosis, and the vascular endothelial cells became loose and disordered. This indicated the cell membrane structure was damaged significantly, while the electrical conductivity was lowered when normal vascular endothelial cells had an intact cell membrane and were lined up tightly. When the red blood cell (RBC) aggregation index increased, the conductivity of the blood decreased. An increase in whole blood viscosity at each shear rate indicates that the deformability and permeability of the RBC membrane decrease.
