At this point, the current easily penetrated the RBC membrane, decreasing in characteristic frequency. The physiological characteristics of vessels and blood were manifested by dielectric parameters. This result provides a theoretical basis for the clinical application of bioelectrical impedance in the thrombosis detection system.

articleTitle: Using IoT Architecture for Remotely-Controlled Physical Telerehabilitation in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Engaging a user in an immersive experience in virtual reality (VR) makes cycling exercise more enjoyable and promotes adherence to daily exercise. Using an Oculus headset, we implemented a Metaverse application for a racetrack game that used IoT infrastructure to obtain and process data from a portable bike in real time. An IoT interface was implemented to support transmission, storage, and real-time visualization of exercise bike speed in an immersive environment. The exercise equipment including a portable bike and pulse oximeter has been successfully interfaced with the VR app providing realtime monitoring of exercise intensity, heart rate, and oxygen saturation and continuous display of these parameters on the exercise dashboard. A dedicated web portal for the clinical rehabilitation team supported individualized exercise program prescription and adjustment based on patient performance. The system allows real-time alert generation based on pre-defined personalized parameters to support adherence to exercise prescriptions and patient safety. The implemented prototype system demonstrated the high potential of Metaverse applications utilizing IoT infrastructure for building scalable low-cost applications for home-based telerehabilitation. The existing prototype system will be expanded in the future by adding wireless physiological sensors, vital sign monitors, and remote communication with the clinical rehabilitation team. The efficacy of the system will be evaluated in a randomized clinical trial.

articleTitle: Impact of Carrying School Backpacks on Students: Quantitative Biomechanical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Heavy backpacks are a common concern for students worldwide, as they affect children's musculoskeletal development. We investigated how different backpack weights, including 0 (control), 10, and 20 % of the subject's body weight (BW), influenced the biomechanical parameters of 20 students (10 males and 10 females) of primary schools during level walking and stair climbing (ascent and descent). Randomized trials were employed in which the subjects performed these activities while carrying backpacks of different loads. Kinematic and spatiotemporal parameters were measured using a 2D motion analysis system and BTS G-Walk sensor. Significant increases were observed at 10 % BW load in trunk inclination angle during level walking and stair descent, as well as in pelvic range of motion (ROM) during stair descent. At the 20 % BW load, significant differences were found in pelvic ROM during stair ascent, and in cadence and speed during level walking. Stride length remains. Significant differences were identified between activities for all parameters, except for stride length. The results showed that a backpack weight of 10% BW or more is not advisable for primary students as it can significantly affect trunk inclination, pelvic tilt, and gait parameters. The results can be used for biomechanical adaptations that could impact musculoskeletal health.

articleTitle: Pairwise Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder Imbalanced Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: This paper performs a classification task on data obtained from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) repository. In real-world case analysis, the number of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients is much smaller than typically developed people. To address this issue, this paper proposes the utilization of pairwise robust support vector machine (PRSVM) algorithms to classify autism spectrum disorder (ASD) patients. In this project's experiments, the correlation matrix derived from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data was employed as a classification feature. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted to compare the classification performance of PRSVM with various machine learning methods. The comparative analysis encompassed various aspects, including different data dimensions, imbalanced ratios, and sample sizes, providing valuable insights into the relative performance of the algorithms under different experimental conditions. The experimental results demonstrate that PRSVM can detect autistic patients more accurately when the data is imbalanced. Moreover, the results indicate that PRSVM outperforms or achieves comparable performance to other conventional classification methods in a variety of situations. Furthermore, our approach can be further improved by augmenting the training set with either exclusively normal person samples or by incorporating patient samples and normal people samples in a proportionate manner. This augmentation strategy holds promising application value, as it contributes to improving the performance and robustness of our method.

articleTitle: Time-Sensitive Tele-Rehabilitation Care System Based on Data Distributed Service and Open-Source Integrated Clinical Environment Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: Taiwan became an aged society in 2018 and will enter a super-aging society by 2025. The medical costs of elderly care continue to rise, hence employing telemedicine is needed to reduce healthcare expenses. Beginning in 2024, Taiwan has integrated telemedicine into home health care, foreseeing a plethora of innovative solutions for inhome care in the super-aged society. However, current remote real-time health monitoring systems are not enough to meet all clinical needs. For instance, during a golden period of 3–6 months for post-stroke rehabilitation, physical therapists require accurate and instantaneous rehabilitation motion estimation data to care for stroke patients remotely, provide consultations, and devise rehabilitation improvement plans. To address this issue, we established a time-sensitive stroke telerehabilitation and remote care system. The distributed data service for real-time system was used for its feature reliability, real-time capability, and scalability, while its information security technology addresses data transmission security issues, ensuring real-time and accurate data with low latency. Open-source integrated clinical environment converts heterogeneous medical device data into a common structure and protocol to exchange data with clinical applications. This facilitates seamless interoperability and enhances the efficiency and performance of medical facilities. Therefore, we adapted data-distributed service technology to establish a time-sensitive system, integrating physiological measurement devices in an open-source integrated clinical environment and building an automatic rehabilitation assessment model with pose estimation to deliver home-based telerehabilitation for stroke patients. This system allows for continuous care after discharge from the hospial, enabling healthcare experts to instantly monitor patient conditions remotely and adjust rehabilitation plans. The system effectively enhances the medical care quality of post-stroke care at home, consequently reducing the cost of medical care in the super-aged society.

articleTitle: Improved Design of Elderly Bathing Chair Based on Ergonomics and JACK Computer-Aided Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 6th Eurasia Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Healthcare and Sustainability (ECBIOS)
abstract: With global aging, the quality of life and health of the elderly have become the focus of social attention. Due to the decline in physical function, the elderly require special care and equipment for daily activities such as bathing. The existing bathing chairs have many issues, such as insufficient comfort, inconvenient operation, and poor stability, which cannot fully meet the needs of elderly users. By analyzing and optimizing the design of elderly bathing chairs based on ergonomics and JACK simulation, the comfort, safety, and ease of use of the bathing chair were improved, which significantly enhanced the user experience and quality of life of the elderly. The rationality of the design parameters was verified to optimize the human-machine interface of the product. Suggestions for further improvement were proposed for the design and evaluation of elderly bathing chairs.
